text:
meena: FYI customer AcmeHealth seeing intermittent 404s on function call after we renamed a tool. They were calling `patientLookup` (PascalCase) but we rolled a rename to `patientSearch` yesterday.
support-bot: Incident created automatically: INC-4827. Assigned to @meena.
jordan: can you paste the raw request + response headers? Hosted or Dedicated for this tenant?
meena: Hosted (us-west). Repro steps I ran against their payload:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool": "patientLookup", "args": {"mrn": "12345"}}'
```

Response (200ms):
```json
{"error":"tool_not_found","message":"tool 'patientLookup' not found"}
```
Headers: `X-Registry-Version: 2024-11-15T21:02:11Z`, `X-Edge-Cache-TTL: 300`
ryan: ok two quick possibilities: 1) alias rename propagated to control plane but edge/regional caches didn't pick up new mapping yet, or 2) case-normalization change in the lookup code (we recently switched to casefold on registry keys). Do you see the old alias in the registry primary? run `registry view-alias patientLookup` and `registry view-alias patientSearch` on our control plane.
meena: ran both:

```
$ registry view-alias patientLookup --region=us-west
Alias not found

$ registry view-alias patientSearch --region=us-west
Tool: patientSearch (id: t-9a8b7c)
Aliases: patientSearch, patient_search
Version: patientSearch-v1
```
So primary has the new alias but old name isn't present. Edge region `us-west-2-edge` still returns 404 when I hit it directly; `registry sync-status us-west-2-edge` shows last-sync 1709423100 (8m ago) and `last-applied`: 1709422500 (15m behind primary).
jordan: that mismatch + edge TTL explains intermittent behaviour while old traffic hits an edge without the alias. We should be able to mitigate by creating a temporary alias mapping from the old name -> new tool and forcing a sync.
eng-ml: note about casefold: we changed matching from simple lowercasing to unicode casefold in the router last week to handle internationalized aliases. If a client sends `patientLookup` vs stored `patientsearch` there should still be a match, but if the registry entry has mixed separators (underscore vs camel) some edge caches may normalize differently. We saw a repro where `patientLookup` didn't map because edge used an older normalization lib version.
ryan: mitigation steps I just did:
- created alias `patientLookup` -> `t-9a8b7c` (hotfix)
- triggered `registry push --force --targets=us-west-2-edge`
- kicked the edge cache refresh (invalidate key prefix `tool-alias:*patient*`)
meena: after your push, I retried the curl and got 200 in 180ms. Response body (excerpt):
```json
{"tool":"patientSearch","result":{"name":"Jane Doe","mrn":"12345"}}
```
Customer confirms success for the last 6 calls. They said they retried at ~1709423650 and all green.
jordan: thanks. root cause: alias rename + edge registry lag + normalization difference between control plane and older edge agent. Action items:
- ry an: backfill job to propagate `--force` for all regions and add a monitoring alert when `last-applied` lags more than 2m
- eng-ml: schedule rollout of normalization lib to edge agents and add a compatibility layer to accept both old and new forms
- meena: follow up with customer and close INC-4827 after 24h stable
meena: will do. closing note for the log: hotfix alias added at 1709423610, sync completed at 1709423670. Marking as resolved pending 24h validation. :white_check_mark:
ryan: also created a short runbook stub under docs/runbooks/edge-alias-drift.md for next time.
meena: thanks all :pray:
